articles.headline: 2026 NBA Finals: Knicks-Spurs Game 5 preview, X factors, MVP pick
articles.description: The Knicks have a chance Saturday to win their first NBA title since 1973. Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs, however, are standing in their way.

articles.headline: Why Victor Wembanyama's most dominant skill remains a mystery
articles.description: What makes the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year so dangerous isn't that he blocks so many shots. It's that he prevents players from shooting in the first place.

images.name: Holmes on Wemby -- lede [576x324]
images.credit: Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images

images.name: Putting Wemby's Game 1 dominance into perspective
images.caption: Zach Kram provides historical context for Victor Wembanyama's huge game in the Spurs' Game 1 win over the Thunder.

articles.headline: Inside the Shaolin monastery that helped build Victor Wembanyama
articles.description: Here's how monks in central China helped turn Victor Wembanyama into what he has now become: the most unstoppable force in basketball.

images.name: Victor Wembanyama Shaolin monks [1296x729]
images.caption: The 22-year-old Wembanyama, after spending nearly two weeks training with Shaolin monks in central China last summer, has led the young Spurs to the Western Conference finals.

images.name: Victor Wembanyama Shaolin monks [1440x1475]
images.caption: The customized training regimen focused on Wembanyama's center of gravity, building strength to endure an NBA that will try more and more to overpower him.

images.name: Victor Wembanyama Shaolin monks [1440x1474]
images.caption: When Wembanyama first learned of the retreat and its program, he was intrigued by the challenge -- by what it might unlock in him and what it might help him let go of.

images.name: Victor Wembanyama Shaolin monks [1066x1703]
images.caption: Master Yan'an and Wembanyama woke each day at 4:30 a.m. and trained and meditated until nearly sundown.

images.name: How Wemby's summer prep has helped fuel his postseason run
images.caption: Victor Wembanyama reflects on how his work with monks and Hakeem Olajuwon over the summer has benefitted him.
